info.name: supabase
info.description:
Self-hosted Supabase gateway endpoints (ai/supabase). Unlike the other collections in this repo, these go DIRECT to the Envoy API gateway on the box — Supabase is not registered as a LiteLLM pass-through or MCP server, so there is no {{litellm}} base URL and no virtual key here.

Set the collection variables before use:
  supabase          the gateway origin, e.g. http://localhost:8022 (PORT_SUPABASE_API in .env). Must match SUPABASE_PUBLIC_URL when called from a browser — Envoy CORS is an exact match.
  anonKey           SUPABASE_ANON_KEY from .env (HS256 JWT, role=anon)
  serviceRoleKey    SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY from .env (role=service_role — server-side only, never in client code)
  dashboardUser     SUPABASE_DASHBOARD_USERNAME (default: supabase)
  dashboardPassword SUPABASE_DASHBOARD_PASSWORD
  table             a table name, for the PostgREST row-read request

This deployment runs in LEGACY HS256 API key mode: authenticate with the `apikey` header (and `Authorization: Bearer` where a user/role token is wanted). The newer sb_publishable_… / ES256 keys are a documented follow-up and are deliberately empty — see ai/supabase/SUPABASE.md § Asymmetric keys.

These are the same requests as SUPABASE.md § Verifying. Full operator guide: ai/supabase/SUPABASE.md.

**Error bodies.** Each endpoint's `#### Schemas` section -- at the end of its first request's description, generated from `supabase.schemas.json` by `scripts/api_schemas.py render` -- documents the fields this stack uses of each response body: an open subset of the upstream server's. Errors answer the upstream server's own error body and are not repeated per endpoint.

variable.description: Envoy API gateway origin. Host port is PORT_SUPABASE_API in .env (default 8022). Use the box's LAN IP when calling from another machine.
SUPABASE_ANON_KEY from .env — the HS256 JWT with role=anon. Generated by ai/supabase/bin/generate_keys.py.
SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY from .env — role=service_role, bypasses row-level security. Server-side only.
SUPABASE_DASHBOARD_USERNAME — the basic-auth user Envoy requires in front of Studio.
SUPABASE_DASHBOARD_PASSWORD — the basic-auth password Envoy requires in front of Studio.
A table in one of SUPABASE_PGRST_DB_SCHEMAS, for the PostgREST row-read request. This instance ships with no application tables, so create one in Studio first.

request.description:
GoTrue liveness. Returns { version, name, description } and 200 once auth has connected to Postgres. No API key required — this is the cheapest proof that the gateway is routing and the auth container is up.

Errors: 503 from Envoy while supabase-auth is still starting (it waits on supabase-db being healthy, which can be ~90s on first boot). Connection refused means the gateway itself is down — check `make logs supabase supabase-api`.

See ai/supabase/SUPABASE.md § Verifying.

#### Schemas

No key.

Response `200` (`application/json`):

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "additionalProperties": true,
  "required": ["version", "name", "description"],
  "properties": {
    "version": {"type": "string", "description": "GoTrue's version"},
    "name": {"const": "GoTrue"},
    "description": {"const": "GoTrue is a user registration and authentication API"}
  }
}
```

header.description: Legacy HS256 anon key. Envoy checks it; PostgREST derives the `anon` DB role from it.

request.description:
PostgREST's OpenAPI description of every table and view exposed by SUPABASE_PGRST_DB_SCHEMAS (default public,graphql_public). Returns a JSON OpenAPI document; on a fresh instance `definitions` is essentially empty because no application tables exist.

Errors: 401 with a JWSError / 'No API key found in request' when the `apikey` header is missing or was signed with a different SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET than the one PostgREST is running with. 500 from PostgREST usually means SUPABASE_JWT_JWKS was set non-empty, flipping it to asymmetric verification — see SUPABASE.md § Asymmetric keys.

See ai/supabase/SUPABASE.md § Access.

#### Schemas

The tables and views of SUPABASE_PGRST_DB_SCHEMAS, as the `apikey`'s role sees them (nearly empty here: this repo creates no application tables).

Response `200` (`application/openapi+json`):

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "additionalProperties": true,
  "required": ["swagger", "info", "paths"],
  "properties": {
    "swagger": {"const": "2.0"},
    "info": {"type": "object", "additionalProperties": true},
    "paths": {
      "type": "object",
      "additionalProperties": true,
      "description": "One per table / view / function"
    },
    "definitions": {
      "type": "object",
      "additionalProperties": true,
      "description": "One per table / view: its columns"
    }
  }
}
```

header.description: PostgREST reads the role from this token. Swap for {{serviceRoleKey}} to bypass row-level security.

variable.description: Table or view name in an exposed schema. Set the `table` collection variable, or type one here.

request.description:
Read rows from one table through PostgREST. Returns a JSON array, capped by SUPABASE_PGRST_DB_MAX_ROWS (default 1000) regardless of `limit`.

Errors: 404 'relation does not exist' when the table is outside SUPABASE_PGRST_DB_SCHEMAS. An EMPTY array where rows clearly exist is the row-level-security signature — the anon role is being filtered by an RLS policy; retry with {{serviceRoleKey}} to confirm. (The same trap is why the Trino reader role carries BYPASSRLS — see SUPABASE.md § Trino federation.)

See ai/supabase/SUPABASE.md § Access.

#### Schemas

One object per row, the columns `select` names (`*`: all); at most SUPABASE_PGRST_DB_MAX_ROWS (1000) whatever `limit` says. An empty array where rows exist is row-level security filtering the role.

Response `200` (`application/json`):

```json
{
  "type": "array",
  "items": {
    "type": "object",
    "additionalProperties": true,
    "description": "A row: column name -> value"
  }
}
```

Storage API liveness. Returns 200 with an empty body once storage has migrated its schema and reached PostgREST and imgproxy.

Errors: 503 while storage is still starting — in this compose file it waits for supabase-db, rest AND imgproxy to be healthy (tighter than upstream, which only waits for them to have started). A persistent 5xx usually means the storage schema migration failed; check `make logs supabase storage`.

See ai/supabase/SUPABASE.md § Verifying.

#### Schemas

Response `200`: no body — the API is up.

header.description: Only required when SUPABASE_FUNCTIONS_VERIFY_JWT=true. It defaults to false, so this header is optional today.
Realtime's tenant API requires a token signed with SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET.

request.description:
The Supabase Studio dashboard. Envoy puts HTTP basic auth in front of it using SUPABASE_DASHBOARD_USERNAME / SUPABASE_DASHBOARD_PASSWORD (the entrypoint SHA1-hashes the password into the Envoy user list at container start). Returns Studio's HTML.

Open this one in a browser rather than Postman. If Studio loads but its panels fail with CORS errors, SUPABASE_PUBLIC_URL does not exactly match the origin you typed — Envoy CORS is an exact match, and a trailing slash is enough to break it.

Errors: 401 on wrong credentials. 503 while supabase-studio is still starting (the gateway waits for it to be healthy, and Studio in turn waits for postgres-meta).

See ai/supabase/SUPABASE.md § Access.

#### Schemas

Basic auth: SUPABASE_DASHBOARD_USERNAME / SUPABASE_DASHBOARD_PASSWORD (401 without).

Response `200` (`text/html`) — Studio's page.
